acceptedClaims.statement:
The matrix in `matrix.txt` is a complete \(23\times 23\) matrix with entries
in \(\{-1,+1\}\), encoded as `-` and `+`. Exact fraction-free elimination
gives

\[
  |\det A|=2^{22}\,3\,5^6\,67\,211
  =2{,}779{,}447{,}296{,}000{,}000.
\]

This independently replays the published lower endpoint already stated in the
problem. It does **not** claim a new record, a stronger lower bound, or
optimality of this matrix.
acceptedClaims.validitySummary: The audit establishes that matrix.txt encodes a complete 23×23 sign matrix and that exact fraction-free Bareiss elimination yields |det A| = 2^22·3·5^6·67·211 = 2,779,447,296,000,000. The factorization and decimal value are independently arithmetically consistent.
scopeQualifications: This certifies only the already stated lower endpoint D_23 ≥ 2,779,447,296,000,000.
It does not establish a new record, a larger lower bound, a stronger upper bound, or optimality.
No external provenance claim is required for the determinant certificate.

value.title: Exact determinant computation for the supplied 23×23 sign matrix
value.summary: For the single complete matrix supplied in `matrix.txt`, exact fraction-free Bareiss elimination yields absolute determinant \(2^{22}3\,5^6\,67\,211=2{,}779{,}447{,}296{,}000{,}000\). This computation is a replay of the stated lower endpoint and is not an exhaustive search or an optimality certificate.

value.title: Fraction-free exact determinant replay workflow
value.summary: Parse a sign matrix into integers, verify its dimensions and alphabet, evaluate its determinant using integer-only Bareiss fraction-free elimination with pivot-row swaps and exact-division checks, and compare the absolute determinant against both a stated integer and its stated factorization.

value.title: Standard-library exact determinant verifier
value.summary: The submitted `verify.py` parses `matrix.txt`, checks that it is a 23×23 matrix encoded only by `+` and `-`, performs integer-only Bareiss elimination with exact-division checks, verifies the stated factor product and absolute determinant, and reports `verification: PASS` when all checks succeed. It uses only the Python standard library.
